title: Basis Arbitrage Workflow
subtitle: A practical reference page for entering spot plus perpetual hedge positions, checking funding conditions, and managing the carry trade without directional exposure.

highlight.label: Entry benchmark
highlight.description: Funding at this level is usually the sweet spot: positive carry is large enough to absorb fees while keeping the hedge simple.
highlight.footnote: Illustrative only. Fees, slippage, and execution quality still decide the real outcome.

monitor.title: Automatic Funding Monitor
monitor.basis_positive: Perpetual premium, suitable for spot long plus perp short
monitor.basis_negative: Perpetual discount, skip this direction for now

trading.title: Basis Strategy Mode Board
trading.summary: Using the current {{symbol}} funding rate of {{rate}}, this board compares estimated yield and trading volume for OKX and Binance in both paper and live modes. It does not jump to the Live Trading page.
trading.okx_paper_desc: Use this to rehearse quantity matching, fee assumptions, and hedge checks for spot plus perpetual execution before committing capital.
trading.okx_paper_note: Best used for pre-trade rehearsal and checking whether funding plus basis is wide enough to cover your configured fees.
trading.okx_live_desc: Treat OKX as the venue for both spot and perpetual legs, with focus on every funding cycle, basis drift, and the resulting net annualized carry.
trading.okx_live_note: The live version depends on both legs filling in sync and funding staying positive. Reassess immediately if basis weakens.
trading.binance_paper_desc: Use Binance as a comparison model to estimate how a different fee and liquidity profile affects volume and net yield.
trading.binance_paper_note: This card uses a slightly lower estimate to reflect platform execution differences in a simple way.
trading.binance_live_desc: Useful for comparing venue-level execution cost and monthly volume before deciding where real capital should scale.
trading.binance_live_note: If Binance execution cost is higher under the same funding setup, net yield will be lower than the OKX model.

weak.note: Fees and slippage will likely consume the carry.

negative.note: You would pay funding instead of receiving it.

precheck.intro: Check the OKX ETH-USDT perpetual funding rate first, then confirm the perp is trading above spot. Positive funding plus a positive basis is the basic setup for this strategy.
precheck.basis_positive: Basis > 0: perpetual at a premium, suitable for spot long plus perp short.
precheck.basis_negative: Basis < 0: perpetual at a discount, skip this setup.

execution.spot_body: Buy 2.5 ETH on OKX spot for about $5,000 using a limit order to keep slippage under control.
execution.perp_body: Short 2.5 ETH on OKX ETH-USDT perpetual with 1x leverage and about $5,000 isolated margin.
execution.sync_body: Submit both legs as close together as possible. If one leg fills first, you temporarily carry outright price risk.
execution.warning_body: The hedge only works when contract size matches the spot quantity. Any mismatch becomes directional exposure.

management.funding_body: OKX settles funding at 00:00, 08:00, and 16:00 UTC+8. Re-check the sign before each cycle.
management.match_body: If the spot and perp quantities drift apart, rebalance quickly so the hedge stays neutral.
management.margin_body: Even with 1x leverage, the short leg still needs enough isolated margin to avoid forced reduction.
management.alert_body: Use an exchange alert for funding dropping below zero so you do not miss the exit signal.

exit.negative: Exit if funding turns negative repeatedly.
exit.low: Exit if funding drops below 0.005% and no longer covers fees.
exit.capital: Exit if you need the capital for another trade or operation.
exit.step_spot: Sell the 2.5 ETH spot position with a limit order.
exit.step_perp: Buy back the 2.5 ETH perpetual short with a limit order.
exit.step_sync: Close both legs nearly simultaneously to avoid reopening price risk.

pnl.footnote: Assumes average funding of 0.02% per 8 hours on a $5,000 short notional. After roughly $10 to $15 in round-trip fees, net annual carry is about $1,065.

volume.footnote: If you adjust the position four times in a month, total monthly trading volume is about $80,000.

risks.capital_body: Spot cash and perp margin are separate pools. Do not assume one side can automatically fund the other.
risks.margin_body: Isolated mode makes the loss boundary explicit and avoids contaminating the rest of the account.
risks.symbols_body: BTC, ETH, and SOL are typical candidates, but always check live funding and liquidity before entry.
risks.market_body: Bull markets often pay better funding. Sideways or weak markets compress the yield materially.
